name: Building Stronger Immunization Systems Through Research

content.title: Building Stronger Immunization Systems Through Research
content.summary: AKU and NIH host dissemination event to advance immunization research.

media.alt: Building Stronger Immunization Systems Through Research

content.text: Department of Community Health Sciences, in collaboration with the National Institute of Health (NIH), hosted a dissemination event in Islamabad on September 26, 2025, to share insights from the project Institutionalizing Learning by Mainstreaming Embedded Implementation Research in Country Immunization Programmes (MAINSTREAM). Supported by the Alliance for Health Policy and Systems Research (AHPSR), Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, and the World Health Organization (WHO), the initiative is designed to generate context-driven solutions, build workforce capacity, and ensure equity in immunization coverage.

Speaking at the event, Dr Soofia Yunus, Director General of the Federal Directorate of Immunization, highlighted the urgent need for collaboration among all partners to improve immunization coverage across the country. She emphasized the importance of transforming communication strategies to counter myths and misinformation at the community level and called for integrated efforts among provincial Expanded Programmes on Immunization (EPI), academia, research institutes, and development partners.

Dr Zahid Memon, Principal Investigator, highlighted the need for bold steps to ensure sustainability of actionable solutions, stressing collaboration with local, regional, and global stakeholders. "We understand the local challenges to develop contextual solutions; working with community and government to implement innovative yet acceptable interventions using existing platforms, providing evidence for scale-up," he said.

The event showcased innovative projects with potential for expansion in collaboration with EPI as co-implementer, including digital monitoring tools in Punjab by Contech International, integration of EPI with health cards in Balochistan by The Initiative, and the use of art-based methodologies to strengthen vaccinators' technical skills and self-efficacy in Sindh under the MUKHTARI project.

The project team, including Dr Wardah Ahmed, Dr Asma Ummad, Dr Majid Tahir, Dr Shifa Habib, Dr Omera Nasser, Dr Najma Awan and Dr Ammarah Ali, played a pivotal role in ensuring the successful implementation of MAINSTREAM. Special acknowledgment was extended to colleagues and technical advisors: Prof Alyssa Sharkey (AHPSR focal person for Pakistan), Dr Zareef Uddin Khan (National TFP), Dr Ahsanullah Bhurgri (EPI Sindh), provincial EPI managers, and Ms Daniela Rodrigues from AHPSR for her technical guidance.
Pakistan's immunization research is now being recognized as a global model, contributing to South-South knowledge exchange and building the next generation of implementation researchers.
